name: ChargeForms
author: Uzair Rehman

sections.description:
ChargeForms is a drag-and-drop form builder for WordPress. Build contact forms, surveys, and lead-capture forms with a fast, modern builder — no page reloads, no bloated front-end scripts slowing your site down.

Free for real form-building:

  • Drag-and-drop form builder with 30+ field types (text, address, ratings, file upload, and more)
  • Conditional logic — show/hide fields based on other answers, with nested AND/OR/NOT groups
  • Multi-step forms with a progress bar and per-step validation
  • Stripe and PayPal payments, including Stripe recurring subscriptions (monthly/yearly plans, free trials, cancellation) — Payment Item, Custom Amount, Payment Method, and Payment Summary fields
  • Entry management dashboard — view, edit, filter, export, and manage every submission from wp-admin
  • Email notifications on new submissions, with delivery logging and automatic retry
  • Native SMTP email delivery — connect Gmail, Microsoft 365, Amazon SES, SendGrid, Mailgun, Brevo, Postmark, Zoho, or any custom SMTP server; encrypted credentials, multiple connections, real test-email sending, and a full delivery log
  • CSV entry import, Save & Resume, and all bundled form templates
  • Webhook integration — send every submission as JSON to Zapier, Make, n8n, or your own endpoint
  • Honeypot spam protection, reCAPTCHA/hCaptcha/Turnstile, double opt-in
  • Lightweight front-end rendering — your visitors never load an admin-sized JS bundle

Planned for future releases

  • Additional integrations beyond generic Webhook (CRM, marketing platforms)
  • Conversational (one-question-at-a-time) form mode
  • AI form generation

External services

This plugin optionally connects to a number of third-party services, every one of them off by default. Full detail on each is in the “What external services does this plugin use?” FAQ above; summarized here per the WordPress.org guideline:

  • Google Fonts — loads the Poppins typeface on ChargeForms’ own wp-admin screens only (never your site’s front end), when enabled under Global Settings. Sends the admin’s IP/browser info to Google on every admin page load while enabled. Terms / Privacy.
  • reCAPTCHA, hCaptcha, Cloudflare Turnstile, CleanTalk — optional spam-protection providers; only loaded on a form’s front end if you enable one under Global Settings > Security. Processes the visitor’s IP/browser data when a protected form is viewed/submitted. Google Privacy / hCaptcha Privacy / Cloudflare Privacy / CleanTalk Privacy.
  • Stripe, PayPal — only active on a form with a Payment field where you’ve connected your own account. Sends the payment amount and the payer’s entered billing details when a visitor pays. Stripe Privacy / PayPal Privacy.
  • Webhook, Mailchimp, Slack, Discord, Telegram, Notion, HubSpot, Google Sheets — only send data if you explicitly connect them yourself under the Integrations screen, to the endpoint/account you configure, at the moment a form is submitted. Mailchimp Terms / Privacy — Notion Terms & Privacy / Privacy — HubSpot Terms / Privacy — Telegram Terms / Privacy.
  • Address autocomplete — optional; sends each keystroke in an Address field’s autocomplete box to OpenStreetMap’s Nominatim API. Usage Policy / OSMF Privacy.
  • chargeforms.com license API — only contacted if you activate a Pro license key, to verify it. Terms / Privacy.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the chargeforms folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install directly from the WordPress Plugin Directory.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.
  3. Go to ChargeForms in your admin sidebar to build your first form.
  4. Paste the [chargeforms id="X"] shortcode into any page or post.
sections.faq:
Is this really free?

Yes. Every feature included in this WordPress.org plugin is available without a paid license, time limit, or submission cap.

Where’s the human-readable source for the built JS/CSS files?

The assets/build/ files shipped in this plugin (builder.js, frontend.js, and their CSS) are compiled by webpack from real, unminified source — nothing here is obfuscated, only minified for production the same way every WordPress admin ships its own JS. That source ships in this same plugin package: see assets/src/ for the real, readable JavaScript, and webpack.config.js/webpack.vue.config.js plus package.json for the exact build configuration and tooling versions used to produce assets/build/ from it. To rebuild it yourself: npm ci followed by npm run build (the admin builder and public front-end bundle) and npm run vue:build (the Vue-based Forms List screen).

What external services does this plugin use?

Google Fonts (optional, off by default). Turned on under Global Settings > General, this plugin loads the Poppins typeface from Google Fonts (fonts.googleapis.com/fonts.gstatic.com) on ChargeForms’ own wp-admin screens only (never on your site’s front end, never on a visitor-facing page) so the admin UI matches its own design. No request to Google happens until you enable it; the admin UI uses your system font stack otherwise. While enabled, this sends the logged-in admin’s IP address and browser info to Google on every admin page load, the same as any page that embeds a Google Fonts stylesheet. Google’s terms: https://developers.google.com/fonts/faq and privacy policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy.

reCAPTCHA / hCaptcha / Cloudflare Turnstile / CleanTalk. Entirely optional, off by default. If you turn one on (Global Settings > Security) to add spam protection to your forms, the corresponding third-party service’s own script loads on your front-end forms and processes the visitor’s IP/browser data per that service’s own terms — Google (reCAPTCHA): https://policies.google.com/privacy, hCaptcha: https://www.hcaptcha.com/privacy, Cloudflare (Turnstile): https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/, CleanTalk: https://cleantalk.org/privacy.

Stripe / PayPal (optional). Only active on a form where you’ve added a Payment field and connected your own Stripe or PayPal account (Global Settings > Payment Settings). When a visitor pays, the payment amount and the payer’s billing details they entered are sent directly to Stripe (https://stripe.com/privacy) or PayPal (https://www.paypal.com/privacy) to process the charge — standard for any WordPress payment plugin. Nothing is sent to either service on a form with no Payment field.

Your own configured integrations (Webhook, Mailchimp, Slack, Discord, Telegram, Notion, HubSpot, Google Sheets). Only ever send data if you explicitly connect them yourself (Integrations screen) — nothing is sent to any of these unless you’ve entered your own API key/URL for that specific service. When connected, every submission’s data is sent to that service at the time of submission: Mailchimp (subscriber added to your list) — https://mailchimp.com/legal/terms/ / https://mailchimp.com/legal/privacy/; Notion (a page created in your database) — https://notion.notion.site/Terms-and-Privacy-28ffdd083dc3473e9c2da6ec011b58ac / https://www.notion.com/trust/privacy-policy; HubSpot (a contact created/updated in your CRM) — https://legal.hubspot.com/terms-of-service / https://legal.hubspot.com/privacy-policy; Telegram (a message sent via your bot) — https://telegram.org/tos / https://telegram.org/privacy.

Address autocomplete (optional). If a form uses the Address field’s autocomplete feature, each keystroke in the address box is sent to OpenStreetMap’s Nominatim search API (nominatim.openstreetmap.org) to fetch matching addresses. Nominatim usage policy: https://operations.osmfoundation.org/policies/nominatim/ — OSM Foundation privacy policy: https://wiki.osmfoundation.org/wiki/Privacy_Policy.

License validation (Pro only). If you activate a Pro license key, that key and your site URL are sent to chargeforms.com to verify it. Nothing is sent if you’re on the free plan. Terms: https://chargeforms.com/legal/terms — Privacy: https://chargeforms.com/legal/privacy.
sections.changelog:
0.270.12

  • Fixed: escape generated form markup, SVG icons, and report output at the point of rendering for WordPress.org security compliance.
  • Changed: CSV entry import, all bundled templates, Save & Resume, multiple SMTP connections, and every implemented builder field are available without a paid license.
  • Improved: the readme and license screen now state clearly that every feature shipped in the WordPress.org plugin is free.

0.268.0

  • Fix: Keep existing Pro fields editable through MCP when a license expires, while blocking new unlicensed Pro fields.
  • Test: Validate structured AI previews and WordPress identifier placeholders.

0.267.0

  • Fix: Pro access requires a verified paid license activated on this site.
  • Fix: Paid expiry is enforced locally; temporary verification outages have a bounded 72-hour grace period.
  • Fix: Display accurate site limits and retry remote site-slot release after a failed deactivation.

0.266.0

  • Fixed: two function signatures used PHP 8.4’s deprecated implicit-nullable form (array $x = null). They are now written explicitly as ?array $x = null — identical behaviour, no deprecation notice. The explicit form still works on the plugin’s minimum PHP 7.4.
  • Improved: the test suite no longer prints deprecation notices from its own REST request stub when run with full error reporting. No plugin behaviour changed in this release.

0.265.0

  • Fixed: a column’s width only ever applied on desktop. The width was printed into the page as an inline flex-basis, which overrides every media query in the stylesheet, so the builder’s Tablet and Mobile previews had no effect on the real form and two-column rows did not stack properly on smaller screens. Columns now carry their width as CSS variables and the stylesheet applies the right one per screen size: tablet (up to 1024px) falls back to the desktop width, and mobile (up to 600px) falls back to full width unless you set a specific mobile width.
  • Added: per-device column widths in the builder — select a column, switch the preview to Tablet or Mobile, and set a width just for that screen size, or choose Inherit to reuse the wider device’s width.
  • Fixed: a column could not be selected in the form builder at all. Clicking a column always selected its parent row instead, so the Column Width setting had no way to appear. Columns are now selectable like any other field, including with the keyboard.
  • Improved: verified the plugin still parses cleanly under PHP 7.4+ and that the existing test suite and build stay green.

0.264.0

  • Fixed: form submissions silently stopped working on sites using a page cache or CDN. The form’s security nonce is printed into the page, so a cached page kept serving the same nonce until it expired (WordPress nonces last roughly 12-24 hours), after which every submission was rejected with “Security check failed” and nothing on the page explained why. The form now refreshes its own nonce when the page loads, so cached pages keep submitting normally.
  • Fixed: the Forms screen loaded about 1.3 MB of JavaScript and CSS it never used. The older Vue version of that screen is retired, but its files were still being loaded on every visit even though the page renders the standard table. They now load only when the Vue screen is explicitly requested, removing that dead weight from every Forms page load.
  • Improved: verified the plugin still parses cleanly under PHP 7.4+ (its declared minimum) and that the existing test suite and build stay green.

0.263.0

  • Fixed: third-round review findings — Notion’s Terms/Privacy URLs and the license API’s chargeforms.com Terms/Privacy URLs in the readme were broken (401/404); replaced with verified-working links (chargeforms.com’s real paths are under /legal/, not /terms//privacy). Added HubSpot’s Terms/Privacy links, which the readme had omitted. Removed the admin-notice-suppression feature entirely (Menu and Builder_Page both cleared WordPress core’s and other plugins’ admin_notices on ChargeForms’ own screens) — not something WordPress.org guidelines allow scoping down, only removing, same as the earlier Custom CSS/JS removal.

0.262.0

  • Fixed: WordPress.org’s automated submission scan rejected 0.261.0 outright (PluginCheck.CodeAnalysis.Heredoc.NotAllowed) — the wp_add_inline_script()/wp_add_inline_style() conversions in 0.261.0 used heredoc/nowdoc (<<<) syntax to hold the JS/CSS strings, which this scanner disallows entirely regardless of content. All 18 heredoc/nowdoc blocks rewritten as plain quoted PHP strings (multi-line single-quoted strings, or string concatenation where a translated value needed to be inserted) with identical JS/CSS content — no behavior change, just different PHP string syntax.

0.261.0

  • Fixed: addressed the WordPress.org directory’s second review pass — text domain renamed to match the reviewed plugin slug (chargeforms), the Custom CSS/JS feature removed entirely (arbitrary code insertion isn’t permitted, only removing it satisfies the guideline), every remaining inline <script>/<style> block converted to wp_enqueue_script/wp_add_inline_script/wp_add_inline_style, two unused core-file includes removed, Google Fonts changed from always-on to an explicit opt-in toggle (Global Settings > General, off by default), four previously-undisclosed external services documented (Mailchimp, Notion, Telegram, Nominatim/OpenStreetMap), and the built JS/CSS source now ships inside the plugin package itself (assets/src/, webpack.config.js, package.json) since this plugin’s repository stays private.

0.260.0

  • Fixed: the live Plugin Check scan’s remaining 18 WordPress.DB.PreparedSQL.NotPrepared errors (entries/forms/form-starts data layer). Two earlier restructuring attempts failed (0.255.0’s variable-held query text, 0.257.0’s single-ternary-of-literals both still tripped the check); the actual fix the scanner accepts is duplicating each conditional branch so $wpdb->prepare()‘s query-text argument is a genuine inline literal at every call site, with zero variable indirection of any kind — verified against the live scanner one method at a time before applying it everywhere.

0.254.0

  • Fixed: every remaining direct-SQL “prepared statement” warning from the site’s live Plugin Check scan (table names built from string concatenation, even though every value was already placeholdered) — rewritten to use $wpdb->prepare()‘s %i identifier placeholder (WP 6.2+) across the entries, activity log, drafts, subscriptions, form starts, notification log, API log, email log, forms, install migration, and legacy-importer data layers. Minimum required WordPress version raised from 6.0 to 6.2 for %i support.

0.253.0

  • Fixed: a few more nonce-recommended/sanitization warnings caught after re-running the site’s own live Plugin Check tool (its results don’t match the automated pre-review email’s tool 1:1), plus mixed line endings in class-email-log.php.

0.252.0

  • Fixed: a second, larger round of WordPress.org Plugin Check findings caught by the tool’s live in-admin scan after 0.251.0’s release — more escaping gaps in field-rendering helpers, a genuine i18n string wrapped in raw HTML, ini_set() sniff coverage, an unprefixed global in uninstall.php, and every remaining direct-database-query/prepared-SQL warning across the data layer (verified safe — each is a fixed internal table-name constant alongside properly placeholdered values, not user input) is now explicitly annotated with its reasoning instead of silently triggering the scanner.

0.250.0

  • Fixed: a batch of WordPress.org Plugin Check findings from the plugin’s first directory submission review — nonce unslashing/sanitization (18 spots), $_FILES name/type sanitization, missing translators comments, corrected phpcs:ignore sniff codes on file operations, Stripe billing-portal redirect now uses wp_safe_redirect(), removed load_plugin_textdomain()/Domain Path header (unneeded since WP 4.6), dropped hotlinked third-party icons from the Migrator tool, added an == External services == readme section, and fixed a dead CleanTalk privacy-policy link.

Older versions

The full changelog going back to 0.208.0 (including 0.244.0 and earlier) is in CHANGELOG.md, shipped in this plugin’s own files (this section is capped at 5000 characters).

Additional opt-in contact integrations

Brevo and ActiveCampaign: when configured and enabled for a form, send visitor email and configured name values to the selected list. Brevo terms/privacy: https://www.brevo.com/legal/termsofuse/ and https://www.brevo.com/legal/privacypolicy/. ActiveCampaign terms/privacy: https://www.activecampaign.com/legal/terms-of-service and https://www.activecampaign.com/legal/privacy-policy. No requests run until connected and enabled, except an explicitly requested read-only connection test.
